reasoning: By the Moore bound for girth ≥ 7 and minimum degree ≥ 3: from any vertex v, its 3 neighbors are distinct, and each neighbor has ≥2 other neighbors. All these must be distinct (from v, from each other, and no two neighbors of v share a common neighbor other than v) — otherwise a cycle of length ≤ 6 would form. This gives at least 1 + 3 + 6 = 10 vertices at distance ≤ 2. Since we only have 9 vertices, this is impossible.
